subject: Re: 3-year commit wallet — escalator + ramp runway proposal
messages:
From: Ellie Park <ellie.park@bitforge.com>
To: connor_obrien@redwood.ai
Cc: lauren_bishop@redwood.ai, rishi_malhotra@redwood.ai
Date: Sun, 9 Aug 2026 15:12:00 -0700
Subject: Initial ask — structure for multi-year committed wallet

Connor / Lauren —

Thanks again for the demo last week. We want to move toward a committed spend model but the procurement team has pushed back on a single upfront prepay for three years. They asked for:

- Year-over-year price escalators (so budget can be forecasted)
- A ramp runway so consumption in Y1 can be smaller and then scale in Y2/Y3
- Clarity on how the prepay wallet is drawn down and what happens if we underuse in a given year

Can you outline a couple of practical drawdown structures (escrow, tranche release, or rolling credit) and the implications for discounts and refunds/true-ups? Attached is our RFQ with expected profile by quarter.

Also note procurement indicated a required SOC2 evidence package and a 45-day standard PO-to-contract timeline.

Appreciate a couple of concrete options and the recommended default you typically sell for customers of our size.

—Ellie
Head of Cloud Engineering, BitForge
[Attachment: RFQ-BitForge-usage-profile.csv (text/csv)]

From: connor_obrien@redwood.ai
To: Ellie Park <ellie.park@bitforge.com>
Cc: lauren_bishop@redwood.ai, rishi_malhotra@redwood.ai
Date: Mon, 10 Aug 2026 08:18:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Initial ask — structure for multi-year committed wallet

Ellie —

Thanks for the clear ask and the RFQ. I took a pass with Lauren and Sales Ops and sketched three options attached (RFQ-BitForge-escrow-models.xlsx) — short summary below:

1) Escalator + Annual Drawdown (recommended)
- 3-year commitment with a declining per-year discount (year 1 highest discount, year 3 lowest)
- Wallet funded up-front but held in escrow; funds are released into an active wallet at the start of each year (or on milestone-based schedule)
- Underuse: unutilized funds can either be rolled forward (12 months) or converted to on-demand credit at a reduced rate (70% of committed rate)
- Pro: predictable unit economics for you; Con: procurement still needs to agree to upfront payment into escrow

2) Tranche-locked Prepay with True-up
- Prepay split into 3 equal tranches billed annually in arrears (or invoiced at start of each year with PO)
- True-ups at year-end with netting (refund or offset)
- Pro: aligns cashflow to budget cycles; Con: smaller aggregated discount vs full prepay

3) Rolling Commitment with Top-up Buffer
- 12-month rolling commitment with a reduction step if you drop below threshold for two consecutive quarters
- Prepay wallet replenished quarterly based on forecasted consumption; surge capacity billed on-demand
- Pro: procurement-friendly; Con: more operational reconciliation and slightly higher unit price

Attached workbook includes modeled discount ladders (3%, 5%, 8% tiers), sample cashflow, and sample contract language for an escrow release clause. For BitForge size/usage profile our math shows the escalator + annual drawdown gives the best blended unit price while still providing procurement with line-of-sight and budgeted annual releases.

Next steps I recommend:
- Quick sync (30m) to confirm whether procurement will accept escrow or prefers invoiced tranches.
- If escrow is acceptable, Sales Legal can provision the MAP draft and escrow instructions; I attached a redline draft (redwood-MAP-draft-v1.pdf).

If useful I can convert the escrow flow into explicit billing milestones aligned to BitForge's PO windows.

Cheers,
Connor O'Brien
Enterprise Account Executive, Redwood Inference
[Attachment: RFQ-BitForge-escrow-models.xlsx (application/vnd.openxmlformats-officedocument.spreadsheetml.sheet)]

Team — forwarding BitForge thread. Quick notes for Sales Ops and Legal:

- Procurement will push for annual invoicing vs escrow; we should prepare the tranche draft that can be invoiced at Y1/Y2/Y3 start dates and include a year-end true-up clause.
- For escalator ladder propose: Year1 = 8% discount, Year2 = 5%, Year3 = 3% (blended to match the up-front equivalency if they funded full wallet)
- Need the following from Legal: escrow instruction paragraph, acceptable language for rolling-forward vs refund, and an optional clause for converting unspent funds to on-demand credit at 70% rate

Monica — can you run a quick cashflow example in our billing model (show both escrow release and invoice-tranche) and flag any tax or revenue recognition implications?

Thanks —
Lauren 
Director, Strategic Accounts, Redwood Inference

From: Ellie Park <ellie.park@bitforge.com>

Cc: lauren_bishop@redwood.ai, rishi_malhotra@redwood.ai, procurement@bitforge.com
Date: Tue, 11 Aug 2026 09:03:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Initial ask — structure for multi-year committed wallet

Connor / Lauren —

Appreciate the write-up and the workbook. Procurement will not sign a three-year single upfront prepay without escrow or a clear refund / roll-forward policy. The Escalator + Annual Drawdown you outlined is the preferred path for internal stakeholders — it satisfies budget forecasting and preserves discount upside.

Can you:
- Share the specific escrow language to include in the SOW / MAP (we need this to circulate with legal)
- Provide the sample invoice schedule so procurement can route PO approvals (we aim for PO issuance within 45 days after final SOW)
- Confirm whether unused funds can be rolled forward for 12 months or if a partial refund is supported and at what calculation

If you can send the redline-ready MAP + escrow paragraph and the invoice milestone table today we'll share with legal tomorrow. Also include SOC2 evidence link so procurement can attach to the PO packet.

—Ellie
Head of Cloud Engineering, BitForge
[Attachment: procurement-checklist.pdf (application/pdf)]
